recipes.name: Game Hen Stuffed with Wild Rice and Mushrooms
ingredients_raw: 1 tablespoon poultry seasoning, or to taste

steps.text: Bring water, rice, and pinch of salt to a boil in a saucepan. Reduce heat to medium-low; cover, and simmer until kernels burst open, 45 to 50 minutes, adding more water if necessary. Fluff rice with a fork; let stand 5 to 10 minutes to absorb any excess liquid.
Preheat the oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C). Grease a baking dish large enough to hold hen.
Melt 2 tablespoons butter in a skillet over medium heat. Add mushrooms; cook and stir until partially cooked and starting to release liquid, 5 to 8 minutes. Stir mushrooms into rice.

Season hen, inside and out, with poultry seasoning, rosemary, salt, and pepper. Lightly stuff hen with wild rice mixture; tie legs together with cooking twine. Place hen in prepared baking dish; add 2 tablespoons butter pats around hen.

Bake in the preheated oven until no longer pink at the bone and the juices run clear, 40 to 50 minutes. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the thickest part of the thigh, near the bone but not touching should read 165 degrees F (74 degrees C). Transfer to a cutting board, cover with a doubled sheet of aluminum foil; rest in a warm area 10 minutes before slicing.

raw_recipe.headline: Game Hen Stuffed with Wild Rice and Mushrooms
raw_recipe.description: Here's a special holiday meal just right for two. A Cornish game hen is stuffed with wild rice and mushrooms, then roasted with seasonings and butter. The hen is ready in less than 1 hour of baking time.

review.reviewBody:
I increased the servings to 8 first. I simmered the rice in chicken stock instead of water. I sauted 2.5 oz of slivered almonds in the butter until golden. I added one pkg of chopped white mushrooms and a cup of chopped onion to the almonds. I added that to the cooked rice. 
Those additions made what was probably a great rice recipe into one of the best wild rice recipes I have ever tasted!

I used the crockpot and added green beans and cream of chicken & mushroom to top them off. 3 hours on high, 2 hours on low and dinner was served. Everyone loved the creamy base with rice and green beans and the herbs added to the flavor. I used 4 hens and generously rubbed them down inside and out with rosemary and thyme. Instant favorite!

Temp too high..reduce to 350. Also, cover the stuffing with tin foil while baking..reduces drying out. If the legs and wings look too brown during cooking..cover them with tin foil. Baste every 20 min. I made a compound butter of herbs d'provance and basted the tiny lovelies leaving out lemon juice (my husband doesn't like savory and citrus)and wine..wine tends to dry out things (as another reviewer commented as adding). Check the internal temp of Stuffing not bird. Juices should run clear. It should read 165 F. Put the birds on a wire rack..setting on base of pan will cause inadequate roasting. If you roast always use a roasting pan or wire rack. I also used a lot of the other comments made and checked online as well.

If you want a more flavorful rice, sautee onions and mushrooms with 3-4 minced garlic cloves. Instead of cooking rice in plain flat water, use half chicken broth and half amber beer. When mixing rice with sauteed mushrooms mixture, add also some dry cranberries and/or slivered almonds. Stuff the hen(s). To avoid that meat/rice dries out, baste hen(s) often with a mixture 1 cup chicken broth, 1/2 cup dry white wine, juice of one lemon and 3 tbsp of melted butter. You won't regret it!

I was craving wild rice and had Cornish Hens in the freezer, but I didn't just want to make wild rice so I tried this out. For anyone who says the bird was dry, you cooked it too long or failed to baste it with anything, it has nothing to do with the oven temp. Modifications: I sauteed diced onions, carrots, garlic and the mushrooms, splashed with a bit of white wine before adding the rice, which I did a half & half mix of brown & wild rice, cooked in 3/4 water to 1/4 chicken stock and a small pat of butter (your measurements will vary depending on how much you make).I left the rice a little watery on purpose- that cooks out in the bird. I do not like poultry seasoning or rosemary, so I just hit the bird with salt & pepper. I set it breast side DOWN on top of some rough cut onions, garlic & carrots, with a few of the mushroom slices thrown in. Roasted for 20 minutes then poured on a mix of white wine, chicken stock, lemon juice & melted butter and let it go about 20 more minutes before I started testing the temp. Once it was where I wanted it, I took it out, set it aside and made some gravy with the pan juices. Again, for anyone saying this was bland, you aren't very creative. The only downfall (if you can even call it that) was that I had too much rice mix. I just put it into an oven-proof ramekin, covered with foil and baked right along side the bird. Served it with roasted carrots and called it dinner :-)

This is a fabulous romantic dinner for 2. We roasted Brussels sprouts with the rice stuffed chicken. I substituted the dried seasoning with fresh bunched together on top of the stuffing. Prepped the bird with EVOO, salt, pepper and herbs de Provence which made it very flavorful, tender and juicy.

I have never really liked wild rice but my husband does so I tried this recipe and loved it! I added sautéed onions, garlic, mushrooms, as well as walnuts and dried cranberries to the rice, salted to taste. Will make this again!

I made this for Christmas for my extended family... first Christmas in charge of the bird/ first Christmas married! Everyone was raving about this recipe! The bird looks so good, and it tastes wonderful. A couple of adjustments I made: I added 1 can of cream of mushroom because other reviewers said the recipe was sometimes dry. Also, I added in the rest of my stuffing from stuffed mushrooms I had made the night before. Combined with a oil, vinegar, and rosemary marinade = perfection!

This is a great meal to visually impress your guests without taking you away from entertaining your guests.

As I am primarily interested in the taste of the main focus, the hen, I omitted the thyme and rosemary. And I added a tablespoon of minced garlic as I sautéed a pound of mushrooms added to the cooked rice, before stuffing the hens.

My brother and I really enjoyed the meal and will be having it again soon.

My challenge is getting that game hen cooked! They always are tough and hard to dismember and I am not sure if this is the recipe's fault or mine. Also, the recipe as followed ends up making way too much stuffing. I cut that in half on the second time around and that worked better. However, I am saving the recipe for the stuffing as it is absolutely superb on its own. THAT I will be making often.

I used this recipe on 2 hens (b/c that is how they were packaged) also used brown rice and used beef stock instead of water and added 1 tsp of both tarragon and sage to mushrooms as they cooked... my husband was IN LOVE!! I'd even use the same seasoning on Chicken Thighs and roast them on finished mushroom rice!!
I made this years ago, and it came out perfect, delicious, and moist. I would like to make it again, but I am not sure if I have the energy these days, but you never know.

This was excellent- I took the advice of Phylicia a previous poster about the almonds and onions added to the rice and mushrooms(I used half white and half crimini). I also made a chicken gravy and added the pan drippings to it. Definitely a keeper!
About the only thing I do differently is I pack as much of the rice/mushroom/red onion mix as I can.
Delicious!

A lot of work for very little meat. Taste was good, but 
i won't make these again.
Great way to really enjoy chicken!!!
This was absolutely delicious! The wild rice paired perfectly with the bird. I added a little feta to the wild rice at the end and my family loved it. Saving this one for the books.
It's a keeper. Came out so good!!!!
No changes made to recipe, was a rather delicious meal for me and my spouse !!!!
